text:
Situation: Heparin sodium has been on FDA's shortage list since 2017-11-14 and remains current as of 2026-10-21. The listing cites manufacturing delays with estimated recovery in late Q4 2026. Current inventory across Corvale sites provides 12 to 19 days on hand at present usage rates. Corvale East holds 61 units at 5.9 days, 151 units at 18.5 days, 134 units at 14.3 days, and 203 units at 24.8 days. Corvale General holds 333.01 units at 31.7 days, 261.68 units at 23.2 days, 167.28 units at 16.3 days, 131.08 units at 12.4 days, and 107.16 units at 10.1 days. Corvale Lakeside holds 25 units at 12.3 days.

Why (FDA record): FDA inspection 925338 ended 2015-05-01 and was classified OAI with six observations including control procedures and investigations of failures, 928 days before the shortage posting. A Warning Letter was issued on 2017-02-14, 273 days before the shortage posting. FDA's shortage posting cites manufacturing delays with estimated recovery in late Q4 2026.

Our position: The approved alternate manufacturer (Hospira, Inc.) provides a direct substitute with no clinical change and should be the primary mitigation. Secondary open-market options exist but lack plant transparency and are not on FDA's shortage list.

Recommended actions:
1. Activate Hospira HEPARIN SODIUM 200 USP units/100mL substitute NDC across all sites — requires approval by pharmacist.
2. Place supplemental orders with BE Pharmaceuticals Inc. to bridge gaps — requires approval by buyer.
3. Place supplemental orders with Cardinal Health 107, LLC to bridge gaps — requires approval by buyer.
4. Place supplemental orders with Civica, Inc. to bridge gaps — requires approval by buyer.
5. Place supplemental orders with Gland Pharma Limited to bridge gaps — requires approval by buyer.

Not recommended: Delaying activation of the approved Hospira substitute; relying solely on current inventory beyond 12 days; pursuing unapproved compounding or concentration changes without P&T review.
